English:
Pet Basics
1. Unlock pets through Pet Search or by collecting enough shards.
2. Use EXP Books to Level-up pets. Respawn refunds all EXP Books used for Level-up and resets the pet to Lv. 1.
3. A pet's base stats are determined by its level and growth rate.

Pet Skills
1. Combat Skill: An active Pet Skill that can be used after the pet enters battle in modes such as Pet Tower.
2. Passive Skill: A Pet Skill that takes effect when the pet is assigned to a Utility slot.
3. Main Skill: A Pet Skill that the Adventurer can manually use in battle while the pet is assigned to the main slot.
4. Stat Activation Skill: A Pet Skill that grants the Adventurer permanent stat bonuses once the pet is unlocked, even when the pet is not deployed.

Pet Rank and Star Level
1. Every 3 pet Rank Ups increases its star level by 1.
2. Ranking up a pet increases its growth rate.
3. Increasing a pet's star level raises the star level of its Main, Passive, and Stat Activation Skills. Higher-star skills provide stronger effects.

English:
In the waters surrounding the continent of Midgard lies a little-known island. It appears on no sea chart, and only ships that have lost their way occasionally stumble upon it. Yet no crew dares linger there, for terrifying, thunderous roars have echoed from the island's depths for as long as anyone can remember.
 
Legend holds that the dragon Fafnir is sealed deep within the island. Once a descendant of the giants, he was slain by a descendant of Odin for his insatiable greed for treasure. After Ragnarök, he returned from the underworld to Midgard, transformed into a decaying dragon driven by nothing but greed. To stop Fafnir's plunder and slaughter, people built fortresses, Turrets, and magic formations across the nameless island. Using gold as bait, they ultimately sealed him away through tremendous Devotion. Thus, the island came to be known as Dragon Sarcophagus Isle.

Centuries have since passed, and the seal's power has begun to wane. The roars from the island grow more deafening by the day, while monsters drawn by the dragon's call gather nearby and relentlessly attack the seal.

Fafnir, the dragon once thought safely sealed away, has lost none of his greed. His power stirs deep within Dragon Sarcophagus Isle, threatening the Peace of the continent.

Faced with this threat, the Guild has issued a call to arms. To protect the continent of Midgard and prevent Fafnir from unleashing another catastrophe, brave Adventurers must be assembled. These heroes will form a dragon-slaying force, travel to Dragon Sarcophagus Isle, and challenge Fafnir once more for the sake of the continent's future.
To restore the seal, keep the greedy dragon contained, and protect the Peace of the continent of Midgard, the Guild must gather the bravest Adventurers into a dragon-slaying force and send them to Dragon Sarcophagus Isle to challenge the dragon once more.

In the spring of the fourth year of the Qingli era@{1}, Teng Zijing was demoted and appointed governor of Baling Prefecture@{2}. By the following year@{3}, the government was efficient, the people were united@{4}, and all neglected endeavors had been revived@{5}. The Yueyang Tower was then renovated@{6} and expanded beyond its former dimensions@{7}, while poems and rhapsodies by eminent Tang poets and contemporary writers were inscribed upon it@{8}. I was asked to write this account in commemoration@{9}.
In my view, the magnificent scenery of Baling@{10} is embodied by Lake Dongting alone. It embraces the distant mountains@{11} and swallows the mighty Yangtze River@{12}, its vast waters surging endlessly@{13} and stretching beyond the horizon@{14}. From morning sunlight to evening shadow, its appearance changes in countless ways@{15}. Such is the grand vista from Yueyang Tower@{16}, which earlier writers have described in full@{17}. Yet with Wu Gorge accessible to the north@{18} and the Xiao and Xiang Rivers extending far to the south@{19}, banished officials and wandering poets@{20} often gather here@{21}. Could their feelings upon viewing this scenery possibly be the same@{22}?
When ceaseless rain falls in dreary sheets@{23} and the sky remains overcast for months on end@{24}, bitter winds howl furiously@{25} and turbid waves surge toward the heavens@{26}. The sun and stars conceal their light@{27}, and the mountains vanish from sight@{28}. Merchants and travelers can go no farther@{29}, while masts topple and oars splinter@{30}. As twilight falls, all is engulfed in darkness@{31}, amid the roars of tigers and cries of apes. Those who ascend the tower then may lament their exile and yearn for home@{32}, fear slander and dread reproach@{33}, and find only desolation wherever they look@{34}, until sorrow overwhelms them@{35}.
But when the spring breeze is gentle and the sunlight bright@{36}, the water lies calm and untroubled@{37}. The radiance of sky and lake meets as one@{38} across a boundless expanse of blue-green. Gulls wheel above the sandbars and come to rest, while shimmering fish swim below@{39}. Angelica grows along the banks and orchids upon the islets@{40}, lush and verdant@{41}. At times, the lingering mist clears completely@{42}, revealing the brilliant moon over a thousand miles@{43}. Its glimmer dances like gold upon the rippling water@{44}, while its still reflection sinks like a jade disc into the depths@{45}. Fishermen's songs echo back and forth@{46}—how could such joy ever end@{47}? English:
The late Emperor had yet to complete half of his great undertaking when he passed away. Now the realm is divided into three, and Yizhou is exhausted and weakened. This is truly a critical moment upon which our survival depends. Yet the officials of the imperial guard remain diligent at court, while loyal and devoted officers abroad risk their lives, all because they remember the late Emperor's exceptional kindness and wish to repay it to Your Majesty. You should open your ears to wise counsel, thereby honoring the late Emperor's legacy and inspiring those of lofty ideals. You should not belittle yourself or make improper comparisons that would block the path of loyal remonstrance.

　　The imperial palace and the government offices are one body; rewards and punishments, praise and censure, should be administered by the same standards. If anyone commits treachery or violates the law, or performs loyal and virtuous deeds, the proper authorities should determine their punishment or reward, thereby demonstrating Your Majesty's just and impartial rule. You should show no favoritism or allow different laws to apply within and outside the palace.

　　Palace Attendants and Vice Directors Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi, Dong Yun, and the others are all honest and capable men, loyal and pure in purpose and judgment. For this reason, the late Emperor selected and promoted them to serve Your Majesty. In my humble opinion, all palace affairs, great or small, should be discussed with them before being carried out. They will surely remedy omissions and shortcomings and bring broad benefit.

　　General Xiang Chong is virtuous and fair in character and conduct, and thoroughly versed in military affairs. When his abilities were tested in the past, the late Emperor praised him as capable. The officers therefore unanimously recommended Chong as commander. In my humble opinion, all military affairs should be discussed with him. He will surely bring harmony to the ranks and assign every soldier according to his ability.

　　Drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men Away was how the Former Han flourished; drawing close to petty men and keeping worthy ministers Away was how the Later Han declined. Whenever the late Emperor discussed this matter with me, he never failed to lament the reigns of Emperors Huan and Ling with bitter regret. The Palace Attendants, Directors of the Secretariat, Chief Clerks, and Army Advisers are all faithful and upright ministers willing to die for their principles. I pray that Your Majesty will remain close to them and place your trust in them. Then the restoration of the House of Han may soon be expected.

　　I was once a commoner, personally tilling the fields in Nanyang. I sought only to preserve my life in troubled times and had no desire for fame or distinction among the feudal lords. The late Emperor did not disdain me for my humble station or lowly origins, but graciously humbled himself to visit me three times at my thatched cottage and consult me about the affairs of the age. Moved by his kindness, I pledged myself to his service. Later, when disaster struck, I accepted responsibility amid defeat and received my orders in a time of peril. Twenty-one years have passed since then.

　　The late Emperor knew that I was cautious, and so, as death approached, he entrusted me with this great responsibility. Since receiving his command, I have worried and sighed day and night, fearing that I might fail in my charge and thereby tarnish the late Emperor's wisdom. Thus, in the fifth month, I crossed the Lu River and ventured deep into barren lands. Now the south has been pacified and our arms and provisions are sufficient. We should rally the three armies, march north to secure the Central Plains, and devote what little ability I possess to eliminating the traitors and villains, restoring the House of Han, and returning to the old capital. This is my duty in repaying the late Emperor and serving Your Majesty with loyalty. As for weighing advantages and disadvantages and offering faithful counsel, that is the responsibility of Youzhi, Yi, and Yun.

　　I pray that Your Majesty will charge me with defeating the rebels and restoring the dynasty. If I fail, punish me for my crimes and inform the spirit of the late Emperor. If no counsel is offered to promote virtue, then rebuke Youzhi, Yi, Yun, and the others for their negligence and make their faults known. Your Majesty should also deliberate for yourself, seek advice on the right course, examine and accept sound counsel, and faithfully uphold the late Emperor's final edict. I am overwhelmed with gratitude for the favor I have received. Now that I must go Away, tears fall as I submit this memorial, and I scarcely know what I have written.
